defect_observations.observation: An explicitly order-level flight-range estimate (inputs 0.4, 1e7 J/kg, g about 10, C about 1/600) is reported as 'about 9.8e6 m'. The held source rounds it to about 1e7 m (printed p. 133, eq. 4.86). This conflicts with the handbook's reporting convention at w02b-p15-073.tex lines 81-90. It lies outside the C04 worked estimate, so it is not counted against C04, but it is the C04 failure pattern (unearned digits).
'About 43.3 K' is given to three figures from F about 0.8 W/m^2, a one-figure input. The body or distance to which F and the factor sqrt(40) refer is not named.
The key-ring calibration is reported as 6.201 (four figures) from l about 0.65 m. The held source reports about 6.20 (printed p. 149, eq. 5.26).

The oil estimate states 'about 3.33e9 barrels per year' from one-figure inputs and attributes the one-figure rounding to the source. It then sets this beside the reported 3.34e9 without stating the precision the estimate itself earns. The distance values 20000 and 30 are listed without their unit (the source uses miles and also offers 30000 km), so the calculation relies on the units cancelling without saying so.

The worked range estimate that carries the input ranges and the omitted-variable failure is built on Mahajan Section 1.2 (printed pp. 6-7, checked in the held PDF). The unit's required extent for the finite estimate example is 'chapter 1 sections 1.3-1.5 only'. The Sections 1.3-1.5 examples in dimensional-and-scaling-inference.tex lines 566-615 (bill volume, train range, oil) get no omitted-variable failure of their own; lines 584-588 only point to this chapter. The C04 success condition is met regardless, but the deviation from the stated extent is left for the user to decide.

Several group counts state the rank, or only the count, without displaying the matrix or checking the rank: pendulum 'rank three' (304-307), drag 'two independent products' (349-351), blast 'rank three' (503-505), oscillator 'two independent products' (664-665), and w02b-p15-073.tex line 124 'rank two'. In the body, a rank check is shown only for the W/m/g example (95-102). This is not the C01 failure condition, because the treatment does check rank.

The rank-nullity proof asserts that row-echelon form has r pivot variables, but rank is defined as the column-space dimension (parts file lines 79-80). The proof does not show that the pivot count equals that dimension. This is a small gap in a proof; C01 asks for an explanation, which is present.

The symbol k means the number of listed inputs here and in the annex monotone-box proof (line 15). At lines 150 and 159 it means the number of base dimensions. The symbol is overloaded, but no unit or variable changes inside a computation.
